To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the West Virginia Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

To the Huntington Police Department Records Custodian:

Under the West Virginia Freedom of Information Act, W. Va. Code § 29B-1-1 et seq., I request copies of the following public records about Terrance L. Taylor, a former Huntington police officer employed from about May 2000 to July 2002:

1. Records showing Taylor's dates of employment, rank or position, and date of separation.
2. Records showing the type of separation: termination, resignation or other. If Taylor was terminated, include the notice of termination and any document stating the reason.
3. Final findings and outcomes of any internal-affairs or disciplinary investigation involving Taylor, including the sanction imposed.
4. Any records of an appeal of Taylor's separation or discipline to the Huntington Police Civil Service Commission, including notices of hearing, minutes and the commission's decision.
5. Any use-of-force or firearm-discharge reports in which Taylor was the involved officer, and any citizen complaints against Taylor with their dispositions.
6. Any notice sent to the West Virginia Law Enforcement Professional Standards program, or its predecessor, about Taylor's separation.

If you withhold any part of these records under an exemption, please cite the specific exemption for each record and release the rest. Under § 29B-1-4(a)(2), the privacy exemption covers only information whose disclosure would be an unreasonable invasion of privacy. Records of a public officer's employment status, discipline and separation relate to public duties, and I would ask you to weigh that.

I'm a journalist with WIRED, and these records are requested for news reporting in the public interest. I ask that any fees be waived or reduced. If fees will exceed $25, please tell me before processing. Electronic copies by email are preferred.

Please confirm receipt. I understand the statute requires a response within five business days. I'm also happy to discuss narrowing the request if that would speed things up.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 5 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Dhruv Mehrotra

title: California Public Records Act Request — Three Strikes and Gang Enhancement Sentencing Data (2021–2026)

communications.subject: California Public Records Act Request: California Public Records Act Request — Three Strikes and Gang Enhancement Sentencing Data (2021–2026)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the California Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

This request covers the period from October 1, 2021 through October 1, 2026 and concerns individuals received by CDCR on a commitment involving one or more of the following provisions:
Penal Code § 667 (Three Strikes law, including § 667(a) five-year serious felony enhancements and § 667(b)–(i) second- and third-strike sentencing) and its companion statute, Penal Code § 1170.12
Penal Code §§ 186.20–186.36 (Street Terrorism Enforcement and Prevention Act), including the gang participation offense under § 186.22(a) and the gang enhancements and alternate penalties under § 186.22(b) and (d)
For each provision above, I request the following de-identified, record-level data (no names or CDCR numbers are requested), in electronic format such as CSV or Excel, together with the data dictionary or record layout needed to interpret it:
Date of commitment/admission, county of commitment, and sentencing court
Controlling and all other offenses of commitment, with the specific Penal Code provision for each
Each enhancement or sentencing provision applied, identified by statute (e.g., § 186.22(b)(1)(A)–(C), § 186.22(b)(4), § 186.22(d), § 667(a)(1), § 667(e)(1) second strike, § 667(e)(2) third strike, § 1170.12), with the term imposed for each
Total aggregate sentence length, and whether the term is determinate or indeterminate (e.g., 25-to-life)
Race/ethnicity, sex, and age at commitment
Current status (in custody, released, paroled, deceased, resentenced), and date of release or resentencing where applicable, including any recall or resentencing under Penal Code § 1172.1, § 1172.75, or § 1170.126

In addition, I request any existing reports, dashboards, or aggregate summaries produced by CDCR (including its periodic reports on second- and third-strike offenders in the adult institution population) that cover the same period and subject matter, as well as the data dictionary or record layout for any offender database from which the above data would be drawn.
Please note that Penal Code § 186.22 was substantially amended by Assembly Bill 333, effective January 1, 2022. If feasible, I ask that the data distinguish commitments imposed before and after that date.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 calendar days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Jenny Wadhwa

title: City Attorney Memorandum re ACLU Concerns, September 2022

communications.subject: North Carolina Public Records Law Request: City Attorney Memorandum re ACLU Concerns, September 2022
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the North Carolina Public Records Law, I hereby request the following records:

One document from the City of Winston-Salem: the memorandum from City Attorney Angela Carmon to the Mayor and City Council regarding ACLU concerns about the proposed “Encroachment Agreement with Flock Safety for the Installation of Automated License Plate Readers (ALPRs),” File 22-0517. The memorandum is referenced in the Public Works Committee minutes of September 13, 2022, page 2: “In response to Mayor Pro Tempore Adams, Angela Carmon, City Attorney, noted a memo that was sent to the Mayor and City Council regarding ACLU concerns.”

For reference: the Public Works Committee continued File 22-0517 on September 13, 2022; the item does not appear on the October 11, 2022 agenda; and the Committee heard it as item G-2 on December 13, 2022. I believe any attorney-client confidentiality for a communication made in September 2022 has expired under N.C. Gen. Stat. § 132-1.1(a).

I elect to receive the record in electronic format under N.C. Gen. Stat. § 132-6.2(a).

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 business days.

Sincerely,

Peircen Lorenz
